en: *New Compilation of the General Catalogue of the Tripitaka of All Buddhist Schools*, Scroll One.
Compiled by the Koryŏ Sramana Uichon. This is a draft manuscript; it awaits future expansion and correction. Should there be omissions or errors, may readers grant them their indulgence.
A copy exists in海东 (Haidong) that is currently in circulation. [Repeated] A copy exists in海东 (Haidong) that is currently in circulation. Scroll One.
The *Great Avataṃsaka Sūtra Commentary* in ten fascicles, and the *Abridged Commentary* in four fascicles;

the above were composed by Huiguang, whom the world calls Guangyuan. The *Commentary* in eight or four fascicles was composed by Huiyuan. The *Successive Commentary on Cultivation* in twenty-two fascicles was composed by Bianxiang.
*Zhengshu Souxuan ji* (Correctly Narrated Record of Searching the Mysterious) in five fascicles,
compiled by Zhiyan; *Tanyuan ji* (Record of Investigating the Mysterious) in twenty fascicles and the *Lüeshu* (Abridged Commentary) in twelve fascicles,
as mentioned above.
*Dharmagarbha’s Commentary on the Revised Determination* (Kanding ji), twenty fascicles;

*Huiyuan’s Compilation and Explanation of the Commentary on the Revised Determination*, twenty-one fascicles (or thirteen fascicles); *Fashen’s Original Commentary on the Reconstructed Exposition of the Perfect Enlightenment*, twenty fascicles (originally nineteen fascicles);
now, the second school: *Dazongyi’s Commentary*, thirty-one fascicles.
Faxian’s commentary consists of thirty fascicles;
Shenxiu’s commentary consists of twenty fascicles, which may also be expanded into forty fascicles; and the topical outline (ke) consists of seven fascicles or more.

Chengguan’s *Sui shu yan yi chao* (Commentary on the Meaning Following the Sub-commentary) in forty fascicles—originally twenty fascicles of topical outlines (*ke*) and one fascicle of the major outline (*da ke*), later rearranged by Shanlai—or in sixty fascicles according to the Jingshan manuscript, or eighty fascicles;

Chengguan’s *Yan yi ji xuan ji* (Collected Records of the Profound Meaning of the Commentary) in six fascicles; and the *Yan yi zhu nan ke* (Topical Outline of Difficulties in the Commentary) in one fascicle.
The above is one fascicle of the *Zhu nan ke* (Sectioning of Difficulties) from the *Xuantan chao* (Excerpts on Profound Discourse) compiled by Dao Bi;
and ten fascicles of the *Zhenyuan shu* (Commentary of the Zhengyuan Era) compiled by Si Xiao.
Chengguan composed the *Keshu* (Outline) in three volumes, including one volume for the Great Outline (*Dake*).
Zhizhao composed the *Lunguan* (Threaded Synthesis) in fifteen volumes.

Zongmi composed the *Shu* (Commentary) in ten volumes; originally it was in eight volumes, but the fifth volume has now been expanded and the *Zongyao* (Essentials of the Doctrine) added to make ten volumes in total.
Wonhyo composed the *Gugeogi* (Record of Ancient Traces) in ten fascicles, or alternatively in five fascicles;

Tae-hyeon composed the *Yakchu gyeong* (Brief Commentary on the Sūtra) in one hundred fascicles; Hyeon-yuk composed the *Yak chingyang daeso chu* (Brief Commentary on the Great Commentary of Qingliang) as annotations beneath the sūtra, totaling one hundred and twenty fascicles; Jeongwon rearranged the *Chingyang daeso chu* as annotations beneath the sūtra in twenty fascicles of topical outlines;
and Jeongwon compiled the *Gamdŏngnon* (Treatise on the Determination of the Canon) in one hundred fascicles.
Lingbian’s *Shulun* (Discourse on the Treatise) in forty fascicles;

Li Tongxuan’s *Helun* (Combined Treatise) in one hundred and twenty fascicles; Zhi Ning’s commentary on the *Helun* appended beneath the sūtra text; the *Helun Yinyi* (Phonology and Meaning of the Combined Treatise) in twelve fascicles;

and Hengsui’s compilation of the *Dabushiyilun* (Great Treatise on the Inconceivable) in one hundred fascicles—of which the first forty fascicles have already been circulated, while the remainder has not yet been seen.
*Fajie guan* (Contemplation of the Dharma Realm) in one fascicle by De Su, with the *Xuanfu song* (Verses on Revolving and Flowing) appended;
surnamed Du, of the secular family, popularly known as Du Shun. *Fajie xuanjing* (Mysterious Mirror of the Dharma Realm) in one fascicle by Cheng Guan.
*Xuanjing yi ji* (Commentary and Record on the Mysterious Mirror) in two fascicles. *Ko* (Outline) in one fascicle.
*De-su’s Commentary on the Dharma-dhātu Contemplation*, one fascicle;
*Zong-mi’s Sub-commentary*, four fascicles; *Outline*, one fascicle;
*Shou-zhen’s Collected Essentials Sub-commentary*, three fascicles.
From [the *Lǎngshù jíjiě*] in five fascicles;
[the *Yǒupéng shùchāo*] in four fascicles; [the *Kē*] in one fascicle;
[the *Hóngjiàn shùzhòuxiūjì*] in two fascicles; and [the *Kē*] in one fascicle.
Jingyuan’s *Fuzhen Chao* in four fascicles;
Yuanzhi’s *Zhiyao Chao* in four fascicles;
and Zunshe’s *Shixuanfu Song* in one fascicle.

One scroll of *Zhu Jing’s Concise Account of the Hand-Notes on the Contemplation of the Dharma Realm* (*Fajieguan shouji*), and one scroll of *San guan zong ji* (Record of the Three Contemplations School);
the above includes one scroll of *Xinzhu fajieguan* (New Commentary on the Contemplation of the Dharma Realm) by Cheng.

One fascicle of the *Lüshi Zhushu Shoutong Jiaoguanshimen Lun* (The Commentary by Master Lü on the Ten Gates of the Thorough Explanation of Teaching and Contemplation); one fascicle of the *Fajie Shidaguanshuo Lun* (Treatise on the Ten Great Contemplations of the Dharma Realm); one fascicle of the *Shiqirufa Jieguanshi Sifamingshen Lun* (Explanation of the Four Dharma-Gateways for Entering the Contemplation of Entering the Dharma Realm); one fascicle of the *Yixiangguanduanmen Zhang* (Chapter on the Gate of Contemplating the Single Characteristic and Judging the Stages of the Three Roots); one fascicle of the *Puguanzhufa Xiangjizai Rufenxiyi Menlun* (Treatise on the Universal Contemplation that All Phenomena are Presently Within the Entry into the Inconceivable Gate); one fascicle of the *Xinfudao Jiao Lun* (Treatise on the Interpenetration of Mind, Buddha, and the Path). The above were composed by Tanyu.
One fascicle of the *Shimen Shixiangguan Lun* (Treatise on the Ten Gates of the Contemplation of True Reality) [is also attributed to him].
*Huan yuan guan* (Contemplation on Returning to the Source) in one fascicle, composed by Du Shun;
*Shu chao bu jie* (Commentary and Sub-commentary with Supplementary Explanations) in one fascicle, composed by Fazang; *Ke* (Outline) in one fascicle;
and *Yi gang* (Outline of the Meaning) in one fascicle, composed by Jingyuan.

*Ke gui shu sanmei guan* (Contemplation on Returning to the Narration of Samādhi), one fascicle; *Puxian guan* (Contemplation of Samantabhadra), one fascicle; *Sekong guan* (Contemplation of Form and Emptiness), one fascicle; *Huazang shijiehai guan* (Contemplation of the Flower Treasury World-Ocean), one fascicle.

The above were narrated by Fazang. Additionally, there is the *Huazang shijiehai zhuban tu xu* (Preface to the Diagram of the Principal and Attendant Deities of the Flower Treasury World-Ocean), one fascicle.
*Huiji’s* *Description of the Diagram of the Flower Treasury World-Ocean*, one fascicle;
*Chuheng’s* *Description of the Ocean of Meanings of the Dharma Realm*, two fascicles or one fascicle;
and *Fazang’s* *Outline*, one fascicle.
*Jingyuan’s Ten-Gate Contemplation of the Dharma*, one fascicle;
*Yixiang’s Commentary on the Revised Separate Chapters*, two fascicles;
*Huiyuan’s Contemplation of the Perfect Accomplishment of Sublime Principles*, three fascicles.

*Shenxiu’s Exposition of the Three Sages’ Perfectly Interpenetrating Contemplation*, one fascicle; *Contemplation on the Five Aggregates*, one fascicle; *Contemplation on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle; *The Definitive Meaning*, one fascicle; *On Whether Eating Meat Is Sinful or Not Sinful*, with an appended *Essentials of the Mind*, one fascicle.
The above [works] have a commentary by Chengguan, one fascicle.
*Tongyi shu zifang yiwang ji* (Collection of Explanations on the Comprehensive Meaning for Preventing Forgetfulness), ten fascicles; *Kaimai* (Opening the Channels), one fascicle;
the above by Wenchao;
*Fajie tu* (Diagram of the Dharma Realm), one fascicle.
*Yixiang Shuzhigui* (The Exposition of the Essential Meaning) in two fascicles; *Fotu Sanzang Shuyangzhizhang* (The Broad Explanation of the Chapters on Meaning by Buddha-tripiṭaka) in one fascicle;

*Guangyuan Shuzhangmen Zakongmu* (Light-Condition’s Exposition of the Chapter-Gates and Miscellaneous Indexes) in four fascicles; *Yaoyi Wendada* (Questions and Answers on Essential Meanings) in two fascicles; what the world calls *Wushi Yaowendada* (Fifty Essential Questions and Answers); *Shixuan Zhang* (Chapters on the Ten Profound Mysteries) in one fascicle; there is also another copy titled *Shixuan Wuaiyi* (The Unobstructed Meaning of the Ten Profound Mysteries), which is suspected to have been composed by a later person; *Sanxiang Zhang Fu* (Chapter on the Three Natures, with Appendix) in one fascicle.
The above consists of three fascicles of the *Jiaoyi fenqi* (Analysis of the Scope of the Teachings) composed by Zhiyan,
and one fascicle of the *Ke* (Outline) composed by Fazang.

*Jingyuan’s* *Shugangmu zhang* (One fascicle), *Zhigui* (One fascicle), *Cailin* (One fascicle), *Huayan zazhangmen* (One fascicle), *Sanbao zhang*, *Liuzhuan zhang*, *Fajie yuanqi zhang*, *Yunyin zhang*, *Fashen zhang*, *Shishi zhang*, *Xuanyi zhang*, *Sanbao bixing ji* (One fascicle), and *Jinsi zi zhang* (One fascicle)— the above were composed by Fazang;
*Mingjian chao* (Two fascicles) was compiled by Mingjue.
One fascicle of Commentary by Yūta;
one fascicle of Commentary by Shōsen;
one fascicle of *Unken Ruike* (Categorized Explanations of Yunjian) by Shōyū; and one fascicle of the Outline.
*Jingyuan shu yidao zhang*, one fascicle; *Dacheng guanxing*, one fascicle—both above authored by Wönhyo;
*Jiu hui zhang*, one fascicle.
*Huiyuan’s Shulüe Ce* (A Brief Compendium of Exhortations), one fascicle;

*Chengguan’s Xingxiu Cidi Jueyi Lun* (Treatise on the Sequence of Practice and the Resolution of Doubts), four fascicles; *Huishi* (Concordant Exegesis), two fascicles; *Lieshi* (Brief Exegesis), one fascicle; *Shimen Xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Ten Gates), one fascicle; *Shier Yuansheng Jieshu* (Explanatory Commentary on the Twelvefold Dependent Origination), one fascicle; *Xianzhi Chengbei Lun* (Treatise on Manifesting Wisdom and Accomplishing Compassion), one fascicle; *Yanmulun* (The Eye and the Head Treatise), one fascicle. The above.
One fascicle of the *Ten Gates of Profound Meaning* (Shimen xuanyi) by Li Tongxuan;
one fascicle of the *Commentary on the Chapter on Clarifying Difficulties* (Ming nanpin shu) by an anonymous author; and one fascicle of the *Record* (Ji).
The above.
One fascicle of the *Chao* (Excerpts) on the "Entry into the Dharma Realm" Chapter by Tánqiān;
one fascicle of the *Jì* (Record/Commentary) on the "Entry into the Dharma Realm" Chapter by Zhìyǎn;
and three fascicles of the *Gāngyào* (Essential Outline) by Yìxiǎng.
Chengguan’s *Jinguan Chao* (Commentary on the Brocade Crown) in four fascicles, or alternatively in two fascicles;
the *Biexing Jingxu* (Separate Circulation of the Sutra Preface) attributed to Dao’o; the *Chongfu Ji* (Record of Chongfu Monastery) in one fascicle;

and Shaoshen’s *Sanpin Biexing Shu* (Separate Circulation Commentary on the Three Chapters) in two fascicles—these refer to the *Wenming Jingxing Xianshou*. Furthermore, there is the *Sanpin Suishu Yanyi Chao* (Sub-commentary on the Meaning Evolved from the Commentary on the Three Chapters) in five fascicles, its *Ke* (Outline) in one fascicle, and the *Xingyuanpin Biexing Shu* (Separate Circulation Commentary on the Chapter on the Vows) in one fascicle.
The above consists of:

*Sui shu yi ji* (Record of the Meaning Following the Commentary) in six fascicles and its outline (*ke*) in one fascicle; *Sui shu ji yi* (Meaning of the Record Following the Commentary) in three fascicles and its outline in one fascicle; and *Ji yi* (Record of the Meaning) in two fascicles and its outline in one fascicle.
The above.

Zongmi composed the *Separate Commentary on the "Chapter on Vows and Practices"* (two fascicles); Zhongxi revised this commentary and annotated it beneath the sutra text; the *Explanatory Sub-commentary* (four fascicles) and the *Outline* (one fascicle) were also produced. Zongmi composed the *Sub-commentary*, which Zhongxi edited and finalized (six fascicles).
Conglang composed the *Vow Text for Arousing the Bodhicitta* (one fascicle).
Chengguan composed the *Separate Commentary on the "Chapter on Pure Conduct"* (one fascicle), its *Sub-commentary* (one fascicle), and its *Outline* (one fascicle).
The above consists of one fascicle of the *Commentary on the Chapter on the Radiance of the Minor Marks* by Lang;
two fascicles of the *Sub-commentary on the Section on Cultivating Loving-kindness* by Wang Shi; one fascicle of the *Abridged Extracts*; and one fascicle of the *Outline*.

The above *Sichao Shuyao yi wen da* (Essential Questions and Answers on Contemplating Filiality) in two fascicles; the *Monk Biographies* (*Sengzhuan*) states that the *Zhui xue wen da* (Questions and Answers on the Cone-Puncture) was composed by Zhitong.
The *Yicheng wen da* (Questions and Answers on the One Vehicle) in two fascicles; the *Monk Biographies* states that the *Daoshen zhang* (Chapter on the Path-Body) is [this work].
According to Dao-shen’s *Account of the History of Buddhism in the Great Song*, in the biography of Yi-xiang,
it says: "Sometimes he took up his brush to write upon his girdle."
Holding leaden pens and leafy tablets,
I have excerpted as if for a formal compilation and recorded as if for a written canon.
Such categories of meaning are designated according to the disciples; for example,
the "Chapter on the Body of the Path" is one such instance.
Or [the titles] may be based on location,
such as the *Sūci-vyākaraṇa* (The Question and Answer on the Needle-Hole) and so forth;
these were merely compiled by those present at that time.
Not yet being proficient in literary style,
the chapters and sentences consequently became vulgar and rustic;
interspersed with local dialects, these may perhaps represent the very source of the Great Teaching.
The endeavor lies simply in following the occasion;
future gentlemen should add further refinement and polish.
*Shiming zhang* (Chapter on Explaining Names), one fascicle, composed by Yirong;

*Kaiding jueyi* (Resolving Doubts on Opening and Concentration), thirty fascicles; *Yaojue* (Essential Decisions), twelve fascicles or six fascicles; *Zhenliu huanyuan letu* (Diagram of Returning to the Source through the Flow of Truth), one fascicle.
The above.
*Yuanqi shu haiyin sanmei lun* (Treatise on the Ocean-Seal Samādhi Explaining Dependent Origination), one fascicle;
*Mingjing shuyao jue* (Essential Decisions by Mingjing), six fascicles or three fascicles;
*Fanyu* (Sanskrit Terms) by Fanyu, two fascicles; *Fanyu* (Sanskrit Terms), one fascicle; *Yinyi* (Phonetics and Meanings), one fascicle; and *Chuanji* (Biographies), five fascicles.
The above consists of the *Lingji* (Records of Spiritual Responses) in five fascicles compiled by Fazang,
and the *Ganyingzhuan* (Biographies of Responsive Manifestations) in one fascicle compiled by Huiyuan.
*Hu Youzhen’s Compilation and Annotation of the Ten Grounds Gate*, one fascicle;
*Anonymous: The Dharma Gate of the Forty-Two Character Verses*, one fascicle;

*Chu Heng’s Exposition on Body and Land*, one fascicle; *Xianshou School’s Resolution of Doubts on the Hundred Gates*, one fascicle; *Discerning the Three Meanings: A Refutation of Opponents’ Questions*, one fascicle; *Responses to the Twelve Questions of Dingshan*, one fascicle.
The above includes one fascicle of the *Commentary on the Ten Mysterious Gates* by Shanchong and one fascicle of the *Essential Points on the Body, Land, and Lifespan*.
The above.
*Zhongxi Shu* (The Reply of Zhongxi), one fascicle;
*Daoshen Shu* (The Exposition of Daoshen), two fascicles on the *Bodhicitta-śīla-mūla*; and the *Imperial Composition:
Praise According to the Chapters*, ten fascicles.
*Imperial Composition: A Categorized Praise of the "Sui-pin" (Following the Qualities)*, one fascicle;
*Recorded by Zhi-shi: A Praise of the "Ru-fajie-pin"* (Entering the Dharma Realm Chapter), one fascicle;
*Recorded by Lady Yang: Ritual Texts*, one fascicle.
*Wangming liewen* (Ritual Texts for the Nameless), one fascicle;
*Fadeng shu shihui zan* (Ten-Assembly Praises Composed by Faden), one fascicle;
*Daoying shu jiuhui li* (Nine-Assembly Liturgy Composed by Daoying), one fascicle.
One fascicle of the *Lizan wen* (Text of Liturgical Praise) by Youcheng;
one fascicle of the *Lizan wen* by Yong’an;
and one fascicle of the *Lizan wen* by Chuheng.
One scroll of the *Ritual for Cultivation and Realization of the Perfect Teaching* composed by Jiaren;
one scroll of the *Liturgy of Homage and Praise for the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter* composed by Chuheng;
one scroll of the *Ritual for Repentance of Samantabhadra’s Vows and Practices* composed by Sanchong; and one scroll of the *Text of Liturgical Praise* by National Teacher Xianshou.
The above is one fascicle of the *Lizanwen* (Text of Liturgical Praise) by National Teacher Qingliang,
compiled by Jingyuan; and one fascicle of the *Lizanwen* by Venerable Fushí, compiled by Tanhui.
One scroll of the Stele for the Venerable Duming Dushun, composed by Xu Kangzuo;
one scroll of the Biographical Account of the Venerable Yanyan, composed by Huiji;
and one scroll of the Stele for Xianshou, composed by [name lost].
*Biography of Xianshou* in one fascicle, composed by Yan Chaoyin; *Biography of Venerable Fushí* in one fascicle—both above composed by Cui Zhiyuan;
*Account of the Conduct of Qingliang* in one fascicle.
One fascicle of the *Epitaph for Qingliang* composed by Qingtan, which differs from the *Biography*;
one fascicle of the *Letter Sent to the Great Virtuous Master of Huayan in Korea* composed by Pei Xiu;
and one fascicle of the *Letter to Disciples* composed by Xianshou.
*Guifeng Shang Qingliang Daban Niepan Jing Yiji* (Record of the Meaning of the Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra by the High Qingliang [Master] Guifeng), twenty fascicles;
narrated by Huiyuan, its outline in four fascicles;
*Wuming Yuanzhi Chao* (Excerpts on the Perfect Meaning by the Nameless One), fourteen fascicles; its outline in five fascicles.
One fascicle of the *Houfen shu* (Commentary on the Latter Part) by Jingkong;
thirty fascicles of the *Suishu xinjing* (Mind-Mirror Commentary Following the Text) by Liangyuan;
and one fascicle of the *Houfen jieyao* (Essential Excerpts from the Latter Part) by Jiyian.
The *Sishu shuchao* (Excerpts on the Narration of Filial Piety) in four fascicles, or two fascicles, attributed solely to Run; the *Shu* (Commentary) in fourteen fascicles, attributed to Jizang;

the *Shu* (Commentary) in eighteen fascicles, attributed to Guanding and revised by Zhanran; and the *Sande zhigui* (Pointing to the Return of the Three Virtues) in twenty fascicles—these and those above.
Zhiyuan composed a commentary in fourteen fascicles (or seven fascicles);
Jingxing composed a commentary in two fascicles (or one fascicle);
and Fabao composed the *Gujiji* in eight fascicles (or four fascicles).
*Tai-xian-shu-yi-ji* (Collection of Explanations by Tai-xian) in seven fascicles;
*Ji-tai-shu-you-yi* (Extremely Great Exposition on the Intent of Wandering) in two fascicles or one fascicle;
and *Ji-zang-shu-xuan-yi* (Profound Meaning Expounded by Ji-zang) in two fascicles.
*Guanjing shuke* (Commentary on the Consecration Ritual), two fascicles; *Fayuan jiyao* (Essentials of the Source), two fascicles—both composed by Zhiyuan;
*Jingang bei* (The Diamond Scalpel), one fascicle.
*Zhanran’s Commentary on the Outline*, one fascicle; *Record of the Manifestation of Nature*, four fascicles.
The above were composed by Zhiyuan. *Summary of the Essential Tenets*, two fascicles or one fascicle.
Wonhyo composed the *Gangmuk* (Outline) in two fascicles, or alternatively in one;
Uijik composed the *Ch’o* (Excerpts) in two fascicles;
and Hyeomam composed the *Yoryeom* (Critical Analysis) in one fascicle.
*Xuanyi shuyi da yi* (A Summary of the Essential Meaning of the Mysterious Unity), one fascicle; *Wuming yizhang* (Treatise on the Meaning of the Anonymous), one fascicle;
*Wuming lizan wen* (Text for Ritual Praise by the Anonymous), one fascicle.
One fascicle of the *Biography of the Late Dharma Master Huiyuan of the Great Sui* compiled by Renyue;
fourteen fascicles of the *Exegesis on the Meaning of the Vairocana-Abhijñā Sūtra* compiled by Dharma Master Meng;
five fascicles of the *Outline* and one fascicle of the *Great Outline* compiled by Yixing; and ten fascicles of the *Explication of the Esoteric* [compiled by Yixing].
The above is the *Jueyuan shu taizang jiao* (Exegesis on the Womb Realm Teaching by Jueyuan) in three fascicles;

Text 1: the *Xiangding fahua jing zhu* (Annotated Commentary on the Lotus Sutra, Revised) in seven fascicles—no author’s name appears beneath the title, but the catalog states it was composed by Sengrui, pending verification; the *Wenju* (Textual Explanations) in ten fascicles.
The *Wenju* (Textual Commentary) in four fascicles and the *Wenju ji* (Record of the Textual Commentary) in ten fascicles were composed by the Wise One;
the above [works],
including the *Zhengan shu pan* (Zhanran’s Determination of Judgments), comprise seven or ten fascicles.
The *Wangming shu* (Commentary on the Names) in twelve fascicles, composed by Jizang; the *Shuzan* (Verses of Praise) in ten fascicles, composed by Huijing;
and the *Xuanzan* (Profound Commentary) in ten fascicles.

Kuiji’s *Shu hui gu tong jin chao* (Excerpts on Synthesizing the Ancient and Illuminating the Present) in ten fascicles, its *Ke* (Outline) in four fascicles, and its *Da ke* (Great Outline) in one fascicle;
the above constitute the *Quan ming shu yi jue* (Elucidation of the Explanations and Decisions) in one fascicle.
Huizhao composed the *Zhu yao* (Essential Excerpts) in four fascicles;
Qiming composed the *Gangyao lüeshi* (Brief Commentary on the Essential Outline) in one fascicle;
and Zhiyin composed a commentary (*shu*) in seven fascicles.
Xuānfàn (Xuanfan) composed a commentary in eight fascicles;
Xuānyī (Xuanyi) composed a commentary in sixteen fascicles, or eight fascicles;
and Jǐngxīng (Jingxing) composed the *Gujìjì* (Record of Ancient Traces) in four fascicles.
*Daobao Shushu* (Commentary on the Great Treasure) in three fascicles, compiled by Daolun; *Xuanlun* (Profound Treatise) in ten fascicles, compiled by Daojun;
and *Xuanyi* (Profound Meaning) in ten fascicles, compiled by Jizang.

The *Zhizhe shuo ke* (Explanations by the Wise) in six fascicles; the *Shiqian* (Commentary on the Subtle Meaning) in ten fascicles; the *Benji shimiao buermen* (The Ten Profound Mysteries of the Trace and the Origin:

The Gate of Non-duality) in one fascicle; and above these, the *Shi buermen zhiyao chao* (Essential Excerpts Pointing to the Ten Gates of Non-duality) composed by Zhanran in two fascicles, along with its *Ke* (Outline) in one fascicle.
*Jizhi*’s *Shibunimon Monshin-ge* (An Explanation of the Textual Core of the Ten Non-Dual Gates), one fascicle; his *Kasha* (Outline), one fascicle;
*Ninyaku*’s *Shibunimon Sōbetsu Shiki* (General and Specific Points of Reference for the Ten Non-Dual Gates), one fascicle;
and *Bontsin*’s *Chū Hokke Honjaku Funimon* (Commentary on the Non-Duality of the Original and Traces in the Lotus Sutra), one fascicle.
*Shōyū Shutsu Jūfuni-mon Kenmyō* (Exposition of the Tenfold Non-duality Revealing the Subtlety), one fascicle, by Shōyū;
*Sho Kun Shutsu Dokujūfuni-mon Shin-chū* (Record of Reading the New Commentary on the Tenfold Non-duality), one fascicle, by Jūken;
*Ji-bon Shutsu Ron-sanzen-sho* (Treatise on the Three Thousand Worlds), one fascicle, by Jibon.
*Injeok seot dab saenggwan so* (Injeok’s Response to the Letter from Saenggwan), one scroll;
*Sanghyeon seot ui pyeonganpim te* (Sanghyeon’s Discussion on the Title of the "Expedient Means" Chapter), one scroll;

*Tanyan shu youyi* (A Record of Traveling Intentions) in one fascicle;

and *Mingkang shu zongyao* (Essentials of the School by Mingkang) in one fascicle.
One fascicle of *Gangmu* (Outline) by Wonhyo;
one fascicle of *Yoryeom* (Examination) by Uijik;
and one fascicle of *Yoryeom* (Examination) by Sungyeong.
*Huiyun’s Treatise on the "Expedient Means" Chapter*, one fascicle;
